name: Kakori Kebab
subtitle: silky skewered mutton mince, perfumed with mace and khoya, that barely holds its shape

ingredients.qty: 500g leg mince, put through the mincer twice

ingredients.note: the tenderiser — do not increase it

ingredients.qty: 2 medium, thinly sliced and fried to brown birista

ingredients.note: gives the fat that keeps the mince soft
the signature note of a kakori

ingredients.qty: a generous pinch, soaked in 1 tbsp warm milk

prepNotes: Marinate the mince 2 hours refrigerated, no longer. Papaya keeps working and past that the meat goes pasty.
Soak wooden skewers 30 minutes, or use flat metal ones — round skewers let the mince spin off.
Chill the mince hard before shaping. Cold mince grips the skewer; warm mince slides.

steps.text: Fry the sliced onion in 3 tbsp ghee over medium heat until evenly deep brown, 10–12 minutes. Drain, cool until crisp, then crush to a powder.
steps.tip: Pull it out at brown, not black — burnt birista turns the whole kebab bitter.

steps.text: Blend the mince with the papaya paste, ginger and garlic to a smooth, almost creamy paste.
Work in the birista powder, ground cashew, almond, poppy seed, khoya, mace, nutmeg, cardamom, white pepper, garam masala, saffron milk, kewra and salt.
Cover and refrigerate 2 hours, then chill in the freezer 15 minutes just before shaping.
Wet your palm and press the mince along a flat skewer in a sausage about 15cm long and 2cm thick, tapering the ends.
steps.tip: Wet hands, light pressure. Squeezing warms the fat and the kebab cracks.

steps.text: Grill over medium charcoal or in an oven at 220C, turning every 3 minutes and basting with ghee, for 12–15 minutes total.
Finish 1 minute directly over high heat to colour the outside.
steps.tip: Watch it — with this much fat it goes from browned to charred in seconds.

steps.text: Slide off the skewer, rest 2 minutes, and serve with sheermal and onion rings.

storage: Best eaten straight off the skewer. The raw marinated mince keeps 24 hours refrigerated; cooked kebabs dry out badly on reheating, so cook only what you will eat.
